newsitem.title: PERU: Peru cenbank creates new instrument for liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Peru cenbank creates new instrument for liquidity.

text.p: The Central Reserve Bank of Peru said in a statement Monday it would use from June a new liquidity-controlling instrument that bought dollars and sold them back to the same financial institutions a day later.
The basic idea was to give the central bank the opportunity to inject the local currency into the system for short periods at times when banks were in need of soles, a central bank source explained.
Under the terms of the new instrument, the institutions selling their dollars would be obliged to buy them back a day later but would receive a commission on the deal, the central bank said.
"The amount involved in the operation is going to be decided by the bank's executive committee and will depend on the circumstances of liquidity levels at the time," the source said.

Peru's economy is firmly anchored to the dollar, which accounts for about 60 percent of all money circulating or deposited in the country. The government and central bank have a long-term goal of "de-dollarizing" the system to allow greater flexibility in setting monetary policy.
